title: Primes Near a Million and Prime Density
full_prompt: Write a ManimGL script that visualizes the density of prime numbers near one million ($T = 1,000,000$). Create a long number line spanning from $T - 800$ to $T + 800$ with a spacing of 50, and add custom tick stretching for sub-intervals. Plot prime numbers in this range as glowing dots (using GlowDots or equivalent glowing circles). Highlight twin primes by drawing yellow arcs connecting them, labeled with a small yellow '+2' text above each arc. Group the number line, prime dots, and twin prime arcs together, shift them down, and apply a continuous updater that pans the entire group slowly to the left to simulate a moving timeline of numbers. In the upper half of the screen, display the text 'How dense are primes?'. After a delay, transition this text into 'Prime density near T' using a transform animation, and draw a curved blue arrow pointing from the letter 'T' to an example label '(e.g. T = 1,000,000)'. Finally, fade out the example and arrow, and write out the approximation symbol and the formula '1 / \ln(T)' to show the Prime Number Theorem density approximation, matching the 'T' from the density label to the 'T' in the formula.

visual_techniques: Glow dots for discrete data visualization
Arc overlays for twin prime relationships

common_failure_modes.pattern: Missing GlowDots class in community edition
common_failure_modes.note: GlowDots is a ManimGL-specific class. In ManimCE, it must be substituted with standard Dots or custom PMobjects with glow shaders.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Incorrect updater syntax causing static number line
common_failure_modes.note: The continuous leftward panning relies on an updater shifting the group by dt. If dt is ignored or the updater is not added correctly, the line remains static.
The code references specific parts of Tex objects like lhs['T'] and rhs['T']. If the LaTeX compiler splits characters differently, this indexing will fail.
